correctness.rationale: For prime p,k≥1, any n>1 with τ(n)|Φ_{p^k}(n) has Ω(n)≥p−1. For p=2, Ω≥1 trivially; prime equality witnesses must be odd q because Φ_{2^k}(q)=q^{2^{k−1}}+1 is even iff q odd. For odd p, Φ_{p^k}(n)=Σ_{j=0}^{p−1}n^{jp^{k−1}} is always odd; τ(n) therefore odd, forcing every prime exponent e_i even. If r≠p divides Φ_{p^k}(n), r∤n and the multiplicative order ord_r(n)=p^k (else the sum would be p mod r), so r>p. If Ω(n)<p−1 then any prime r|τ(n)=Π(e_i+1) satisfies r≤e_i+1≤Ω+1<p, contradicting cyclotomic order. At Ω=p−1 all primes in τ(n) must equal p, hence e_i+1=p and exactly one factor q^{p−1}; q≠p because Φ_{p^k}(q^{p−1})≡1 mod p if q=p. Conversely for q≠p, Fermat gives q^{p−1}≡1 mod p and Φ_{p^k}(q^{p−1})≡p≡0 mod p=τ(q^{p−1}). The proof is uniform in k and q. Independent divisibility checks for n up to 5000 on sampled p,k reproduced 2054 relative hits and 1384 boundary instances; they do not establish the infinite theorem.

evidence: If Q(1)=p>1, general construction yields witnesses q^{p−1} for suitable q, but does not exclude arbitrary n with smaller Ω.

originality.rationale: Abel–Lauer–Redi (2021) Corollary 2 specifically gives infinitely many τ-numbers relative to Φ_{p^k} using the general condition Φ_{p^k}(1)=p. It constructs exponent p−1 witnesses from a congruence progression, but does not prove Ω≥p−1 for all nontrivial solutions, classify all equality cases, or allow every prime q≠p at the extremal layer. Zelinsky 2002 introduced polynomial-relative τ-numbers and an overbroad infinitude assertion later repaired. A related published SCOPE theorem for Φ_{2p^k} concerns a different cyclotomic family with a unique trivial solution, so it does not imply this one. Result is a sharp natural multiplicity boundary, with priority risk from classical cyclotomic order folklore.
residual_risks: The cyclotomic order argument is short and could be known in arithmetic folklore or a source not indexed with relative τ terminology.
The classification addresses only the minimum Ω layer, not all solutions at larger multiplicity.

value.rationale: Prime-power cyclotomic polynomials are explicitly singled out in the original relative-τ literature, and Ω is the canonical complexity measure counting prime factors with multiplicity. The theorem proves that p−1 is an intrinsic minimum, not an artifact of a witness construction, and classifies every equality case for all k. It identifies an exact natural invariant over an infinite parameter family, with nonexistence below the boundary.

limitations: Only Φ_{p^k}, not Φ_{2p^k} nor arbitrary integer polynomials.
The finite regression is not used as a general impossibility proof.
